subject: Archaeology
subcategory: Lost Cities of the Ancient World
title: Dunhuang: The Silk Road Oasis
description: A 60-second lesson on Dunhuang: The Silk Road Oasis.

hook.text: A Taoist monk stumbled into a sealed cave in China and found 50,000 ancient documents hidden inside.

buildup.text: Dunhuang was a key Silk Road stop. Buddhist monks carved 492 caves into the cliffs and filled them with art.

discovery.text: The Library Cave, sealed around 1000 CE, contained the world's oldest printed book — the Diamond Sutra from 868 CE.

twist.text: British explorer Aurel Stein bought thousands of manuscripts for a tiny fee. China calls it cultural theft.

climax.text: The documents are now split between London, Paris, Beijing, and St. Petersburg. No single place holds them all.

punchline.text: A monk opened a cave. The world's oldest printed book fell out.

quiz.question: What was found in the sealed Library Cave at Dunhuang?
options: Thousands of jade artifacts from the Han Dynasty
50,000 documents including the world's oldest printed book
Silk garments preserved in perfect condition
